paper_title: A Compact Index for Cartesian Tree Matching
statement: Can we achieve 2n + o(n) bits? We need to achieve 2n + o(n) bits to make it succinct (L) regarding the entropy bound of Cartesian trees. We do not think that Bk can be further (F ) reduced, but we think Bk can be represented in a space-efficient way. Nevertheless, it (F ) seems quite challenging to represent Bk within o(n) bits to achieve succinctness.
context: We also have open problems that should be addressed in the future work as follows: Can we achieve 2n + o(n) bits? We need to achieve 2n + o(n) bits to make it succinct (L) regarding the entropy bound of Cartesian trees. We do not think that Bk can be further (F ) reduced, but we think Bk can be represented in a space-efficient way. Nevertheless, it (F ) seems quite challenging to represent Bk within o(n) bits to achieve succinctness. Can we efficiently locate the occurrences? The standard method that uses a sampled suffix array may take a long time especially when a pattern is long and it is also very frequent, because the time complexity has an O(|P | · occ) term, which would result in O(n2 ) time for locating occurrences. Although it might be a rare case in practice, the algorithm should be improved in order to bound the worst case complexity. Can we apply the trimmed LF-mapping to other indexing problems? We may apply the trimmed LF-mapping when L-values or pattern lengths are bounded by O(1).
